name: Open carpal tunnel approach
corridor: Direct palmar exposure of the transverse carpal ligament for median-nerve decompression

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm supported on a hand table and the hand accessible to the surgeon.

setup.text: Confirm laterality, anesthesia and tourniquet plan, and prepare the distal forearm and hand so exposure can be extended if needed.

surface_landmarks.text: Orient to the thenar and hypothenar landmarks, wrist crease, and palmaris longus when present.

incision.text: Use the supervising surgeon's palmar incision and develop the superficial exposure with careful protection of cutaneous branches.

superficial_interval.text: Proceed through skin, subcutaneous tissue, and palmar fascia while protecting superficial sensory branches.

deep_interval.text: Identify the transverse carpal ligament directly and release it under controlled visualization with the median nerve deep to it.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, palmar fascia, transverse carpal ligament, then carpal-tunnel contents.

structures_encountered.text: Palmar fascia and transverse carpal ligament are encountered before the median nerve and flexor tendons within the tunnel.

structures_at_risk.text: Protect the median nerve, recurrent motor branch, palmar cutaneous branch, superficial palmar arch, flexor tendons, and ulnar neurovascular bundle.

danger_zones.text: Blind distal advancement risks the superficial palmar arch and a variant recurrent motor branch; uncontrolled radial cutting risks the motor branch.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid aggressive median-nerve manipulation and stop when unexpected neural tissue or uncertain anatomy is encountered.

exposure.text: The open approach provides direct visualization of the transverse carpal ligament and its proximal and distal release endpoints.

limitations.text: The incision and superficial dissection may contribute to scar sensitivity or pillar pain.

extensions.text: Extend exposure under direct vision when the release endpoint or anatomy cannot be confirmed safely.

indications.text: Use when open release is selected for median-nerve decompression or when direct visualization is preferred or required.

relative_contraindications.text: Reconsider routine elective release when diagnosis is uncertain, infection or uncontrolled medical risk is present, or postoperative care cannot be followed.

closure.text: Confirm complete release and hemostasis, then close and dress according to tissue condition and surgeon preference.

complications.text: Failure modes include incomplete release, nerve-branch injury, vascular or tendon injury, hematoma, infection, scar sensitivity, pillar pain, and stiffness.

bailouts.text: If anatomy is uncertain or an injury is suspected, stop, improve direct exposure, and obtain attending assessment before proceeding.

questions.question: What is the essential endpoint?
questions.answer: Complete proximal-to-distal release of the transverse carpal ligament without injury to the median nerve or adjacent structures.

questions.question: Why is the recurrent motor branch at risk?
questions.answer: Its distal course varies and may be subligamentous or transligamentous, placing it in the path of uncontrolled distal or radial release.

questions.question: Why can sensation over the thenar palm be injured?
questions.answer: The palmar cutaneous branch travels superficial to the flexor retinaculum and can be injured during superficial exposure.
